{{Short description|Architectural instruction}}
{{More footnotes needed|date=December 2013}}
{{for|the fighter aircraft|F-16C}}
The '''F16C'''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://walbourn.github.io/directxmath-f16c-and-fma/|title=DirectXMath: F16C and FMA|author=Chuck Walbourn|date=September 11, 2012}}</ref> (previously/informally known as '''CVT16''') instruction set is an [[x86]] [[instruction set architecture]] extension which provides support for converting between [[half-precision]] and standard IEEE [[single-precision floating-point format]]s.

== History ==
The CVT16 instruction set, announced by [[Advanced Micro Devices|AMD]] on May 1, 2009,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://support.amd.com/us/Processor_TechDocs/43479.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090520223024/http://support.amd.com/us/Processor_TechDocs/43479.pdf |archive-date=2009-05-20  | accessdate = 2022-07-05 | work = AMD64 Architecture Programmer's Manual | title = 128-Bit and 256-Bit XOP, FMA4 and CVT16 Instructions | volume = 6 | date = 2009-05-01 }}</ref> is an extension to the 128-bit [[Streaming SIMD Extensions|SSE]] core instructions in the [[x86]] and [[AMD64]] instruction sets.

CVT16 is a revision of part of the [[SSE5]] instruction set proposal announced on August 30, 2007, which is supplemented by the [[XOP instruction set|XOP]] and [[FMA instruction set|FMA4]] instruction sets. This revision makes the binary coding of the proposed new instructions more compatible with [[Intel]]'s [[Advanced Vector Extensions|AVX]] instruction extensions, while the functionality of the instructions is unchanged.

In recent documents, the name F16C is formally used in both [[Intel]] and [[AMD]] [[x86-64]] architecture specifications.

==Technical information==
There are variants that convert four floating-point values in an [[Streaming SIMD Extensions#Registers|XMM register]] or 8 floating-point values in a [[Advanced Vector Extensions|YMM register]].

The instructions are abbreviations for "vector convert packed half to packed single" and vice versa:

* <code>VCVTPH2PS xmmreg,xmmrm64</code>{{snd}} convert four half-precision floating point values in memory or the bottom half of an XMM register to four single-precision floating-point values in an XMM register.
* <code>VCVTPH2PS ymmreg,xmmrm128</code>{{snd}} convert eight half-precision floating point values in memory or an XMM register (the bottom half of a YMM register) to eight single-precision floating-point values in a YMM register.
* <code>VCVTPS2PH xmmrm64,xmmreg,imm8</code>{{snd}} convert four single-precision floating point values in an XMM register to half-precision floating-point values in memory or the bottom half an XMM register.
* <code>VCVTPS2PH xmmrm128,ymmreg,imm8</code>{{snd}} convert eight single-precision floating point values in a YMM register to half-precision floating-point values in memory or an XMM register.

The 8-bit immediate argument to <code>VCVTPS2PH</code> selects the [[rounding]] mode.  Values 0–4 select nearest, down, up, truncate, and the mode set in <code>MXCSR.RC</code>.

Support for these instructions is indicated by bit 29 of ECX after [[CPUID#EAX=1: Processor Info and Feature Bits|CPUID with EAX=1]].

== CPUs with F16C ==

* [[Advanced Micro Devices|AMD]]:
** [[Jaguar (microarchitecture)|Jaguar-based]] processors
** [[Puma (microarchitecture)|Puma-based]] processors
** "Heavy Equipment" processors 
*** [[Piledriver (microarchitecture)|Piledriver-based]] processors, Q4 2012<ref>{{citation |url= http://developer.amd.com/wordpress/media/2012/10/New-Bulldozer-and-Piledriver-Instructions.pdf |title= New "Bulldozer" and "Piledriver" Instructions |publisher= AMD |date= October 2012}}</ref>
*** [[Steamroller (microarchitecture)|Steamroller-based]] processors, Q1 2014
*** [[Excavator (microarchitecture)|Excavator-based]] processors, Q2 2015
** [[Zen (microarchitecture)|Zen-based]] processors, Q1 2017, and newer
* [[Intel Corporation|Intel]]:
** [[Ivy Bridge (microarchitecture)|Ivy Bridge]] processors and newer
